---
title: Retries, redelivery and secret rotation
description: How ClipMux retries a failed webhook for 24 hours, how to send one again, and how to change a webhook secret without losing events.
---

A webhook that fails isn't lost at once. ClipMux retries it on a schedule
for 24 hours, backs off from an endpoint that keeps failing, and keeps a
log of every delivery that the server's owner can read and redeliver from
the dashboard. This page covers that schedule, redelivery, and changing an
endpoint's secret with no downtime.

## Before you start

- A webhook endpoint for your app; see [Receive webhooks](/docs/build/webhooks).
- For redelivery and rotation, the owner's account on the ClipMux server.
  These are owner actions in the dashboard; an API key can't reach them.

## What counts as delivered

Any `2xx` answer within 10 seconds. Everything else is a failure: another
status, a redirect (never followed), a timeout, or a connection that
fails. Each try is signed with a fresh timestamp, and every try of the same
event has the same `X-Webhook-Id`.

## The retry schedule

After a failed try, ClipMux waits, then tries again:

| Try | About this long after the event |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | at once |
| 2 | 30 seconds |
| 3 | 2½ minutes |
| 4 | 12½ minutes |
| 5 | 42½ minutes |
| 6 | 1 hour 42½ minutes |
| 7 | 3 hours 42½ minutes |
| 8 | 7 hours 42½ minutes |
| 9 | 15 hours 42½ minutes |
| 10 | 23 hours 42½ minutes |
| 11 | 24 hours, the last |

After the last try fails, the delivery is marked `failed`. Your
[catch-up job](/docs/build/webhooks) picks up anything you missed, or the
owner can redeliver it.

Events are delivered independently, so a failing one doesn't hold up the
next, and they can arrive out of order.

## When an endpoint keeps failing

After 5 failed tries in a row to the same endpoint, ClipMux stops sending
to it for a minute, then for twice as long after each further failure, up
to an hour. Deliveries skipped this way aren't charged a try, and their
24-hour window doesn't move, so an endpoint that comes back catches up. One
success resets the count.

In the dashboard, an endpoint shows **Healthy**, the number of failures in
a row, or **Paused after N failures** while it's being skipped.

## See deliveries and redeliver

Under **Apps & API**, open your app, then **Webhooks**, and choose
**Deliveries** on an endpoint. The latest 100 deliveries show their event
type, HTTP status or error (`timeout`, `connection_failed`, `http_500` and
so on), how many tries they took, and when the next try is due. A delivery
that gave up has **Redeliver**: it's retried on the same schedule for a
fresh 24 hours.

The same as owner routes:

- `GET /v1/webhook-endpoints/{id}/deliveries` lists the latest 100, each
  with `status` (`pending`, `delivered` or `failed`), `attempts`,
  `last_status`, `last_error` and `next_attempt_at`.
- `POST /v1/webhook-deliveries/{id}/redeliver` answers `202` for a `failed`
  delivery, and `409 not_redeliverable` for any other.

Since delivery is at least once, a redelivered event may be one your
handler already applied. An idempotent handler doesn't care.

## Rotate a secret with no downtime

An endpoint can hold a new secret beside the current one. Deliveries stay
signed with the current secret until you activate the new one, so you can
deploy first and switch after.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Create the new secret

In the dashboard, choose **Rotate secret** on the endpoint, or call
`POST /v1/webhook-endpoints/{id}/secret`, which answers
`201 {"secret": "whsec_…", "active": false}`. The secret is shown once;
copy it into your secret store.

</Step>
<Step>

### Deploy a verifier that accepts both

Deploy your app so it accepts the new secret and the current one. With the
Node SDK, try one, then the other:

```ts title="webhook.ts"
import { verifyWebhook, WebhookVerificationError } from '@clipmux/node'

async function verifyEither(raw: string, headers: Headers) {
  try {
    return await verifyWebhook(process.env.CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET!, raw, headers) // the new secret
  } catch (err) {
    const previous = process.env.PREVIOUS_WEBHOOK_SECRET
    if (!(err instanceof WebhookVerificationError) || err.reason !== 'bad_signature' || !previous) throw err
    return verifyWebhook(previous, raw, headers)
  }
}
```

The Python, Go and PHP functions in
[Verify webhook signatures](/docs/build/webhooks/verify-signatures) work the
same way: call them with the new secret, and on `bad_signature` with the
old one.

</Step>
<Step>

### Activate it

Choose **Activate new secret** in the dashboard, or call
`POST /v1/webhook-endpoints/{id}/secret/activate`, which answers
`{"active": true}`. From the next try, deliveries are signed with the new
secret, retries of older events included. Without a waiting secret it
answers `409 no_pending_secret`.

</Step>
<Step>

### Drop the old secret

Once you've seen deliveries verify with the new secret, remove the old one
from your app.

</Step>
</Steps>

`clipmuxHandler` verifies with one secret. If you use it, set
`CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to the new secret, deploy, and activate right
after. Deliveries that arrive in between fail and are retried, so nothing
is lost; they arrive a little late.

If a secret leaked, rotate it the same way, and activate as soon as your
app accepts the new one.

## Check it works

After activating, open **Deliveries**: new deliveries show `200`. A row
with `400` means your app is still checking only the old secret, or not yet
the new one.
